column1:
- Core FOMC message: Labor market remains strong with low unemployment; overall activity has slowed from Q4; inflation is muted near 2% (ex-food/energy); Committee held rates at 2-1/4 to 2-1/2% and will be patient amid global/financial headwinds.
- Beige Book overlay: Tight labor markets with widespread worker shortages (IT, manufacturing, trucking, restaurants, construction) and continued wage gains across skill tiers; firms used non-wage compensation to attract/retain workers.
- Demand/momentum: Retail/auto/tourism activity present but household spending slowed early in the year, partly reflecting harsh winter weather and higher credit costs; real estate mixed.
- Manufacturing: Softer tone tied to weaker global demand, tariffs, and trade policy uncertainty.
- Credit conditions (SLOOS): Tighter standards and wider spreads for C&I and construction/land development; weaker demand across residential real estate and HELOCs; banks expected further tightening in 2019 for C&I/CRE and deterioration among nonprime borrowers and some mortgages. This points to a less supportive credit channel than the macro baseline alone suggests.
- Other early-2019 drags: Government shutdown effects noted in January/February.
- Policy implication: Beige Book and SLOOS reinforce a risk‑management, patient stance—solid labor backdrop but softer spending/investment and tighter credit tilt risks modestly to the downside.

Net tone: cautious with a modest downside skew; slightly weaker than a pure macro read.
